title: Vespasian reaches Jericho; Qumran likely destroyed
note: Josephus dates Vespasian's arrival at Jericho to 3 Daisios; archaeologists tie the burning of Khirbet Qumran to this campaign. The day is Josephus's, the link to Qumran is inferred, and the Julian equivalent depends on how his Macedonian months are converted (often 21 June).

title: Ginsburg declares the Shapira Deuteronomy strips a forgery
note: Christian David Ginsburg of the British Museum published his judgment that the leather strips Moses Shapira said came from near the Dead Sea were fake, a verdict some scholars now question in light of Qumran.

title: Moses Shapira dies in Rotterdam
note: Disgraced after his scroll was rejected, the Jerusalem antiquities dealer took his own life in a Rotterdam hotel; the strips later vanished after an 1885 sale.

title: Sukenik buys the first scrolls in Bethlehem
note: Eleazar Sukenik of the Hebrew University crossed to Bethlehem and bought Cave 1 scrolls for the Jewish people on the very day the UN voted to partition Palestine.

title: Sukenik acquires another Cave 1 scroll
note: Less than a month after his first purchase, Sukenik obtained a further scroll from the same Bethlehem source, completing the Hebrew University's set of three.
source: Schiffman, Reclaiming the Dead Sea Scrolls

title: John Trever photographs the scrolls at ASOR
note: At the American School of Oriental Research, John Trever photographed the Great Isaiah Scroll, the Community Rule and the Habakkuk Commentary brought from St Mark's Monastery. He worked with them over roughly 18 to 21 February; 21 February is the date usually given.

title: Albright hails the greatest manuscript find of modern times
note: After seeing Trever's prints, William F. Albright wrote back congratulating him on what he called the greatest manuscript discovery of modern times. The original letter is dated 8 March 1948.

title: ASOR and Yale announce the discovery to the world
note: Millar Burrows of ASOR issued the press release, through Yale, that first made the scrolls public news. Most sources give 11 April; John J. Collins dates the Yale News Bureau release to 10 April.
source: Wikipedia; Collins, The Dead Sea Scrolls: A Biography

title: Sukenik announces the Hebrew University scrolls
note: Two weeks after the American announcement, Sukenik issued his own statement about the scrolls he had bought for the Hebrew University.

title: Cave 1 located by Lippens and el-Zebn
note: Belgian UN observer Captain Philippe Lippens and Arab Legion Captain Akkash el-Zebn found the cave where the first scrolls had been discovered.

title: Mar Samuel takes four scrolls to the United States
note: The Syrian Metropolitan Athanasius Yeshue Samuel left for America with his four Cave 1 scrolls to exhibit them and find a buyer. Sources agree on January 1949; the day comes from a single chronology.

title: Harding and de Vaux begin excavating Cave 1
note: The Jordanian Department of Antiquities and the Ecole Biblique, led by G. Lankester Harding and Roland de Vaux, dug Cave 1 from 15 February to 5 March, recovering fragments and pottery.

title: First US exhibition of the scrolls opens at the Library of Congress
note: Three of Mar Samuel's scrolls went on show at the Library of Congress, opening to invited guests and to the public the next day.

title: Libby radiocarbon-dates Cave 1 linen
note: Willard Libby tested linen wrapping from Cave 1 in one of the earliest archaeological uses of radiocarbon dating, placing it around the turn of the era.
source: Wikipedia: Carbon dating the Dead Sea Scrolls

title: First excavation season at Khirbet Qumran
note: De Vaux and Harding began digging the ruins beside the caves, a season that ran to 12 December and linked the settlement to the scroll jars.
source: Schiffman, Reclaiming the Dead Sea Scrolls

title: Copper Scroll found in Cave 3
note: An ASOR and Ecole Biblique survey entered Cave 3 and found two rolled copper sheets listing hidden treasure, along with other fragments.

title: Cave 4 excavated by Harding, de Vaux and Milik
note: After Bedouin looted the richest cave of all, archaeologists excavated Cave 4 from 22 to 29 September, recovering part of a trove of some 15,000 fragments.

title: Eleazar Sukenik dies
note: The archaeologist who first recognized the scrolls' age and bought three of them died in Jerusalem, before his son could bring the rest to Israel.

title: Scrolls advertised for sale in the Wall Street Journal
note: A classified notice headed "The Four Dead Sea Scrolls" offered Mar Samuel's manuscripts for sale; Yigael Yadin, then in the US, learned of it and arranged a secret purchase.

title: Four scrolls bought for Israel at the Waldorf-Astoria
note: The scrolls were handed over at the Waldorf-Astoria and bought through intermediaries for $250,000 on behalf of Yadin and the State of Israel.

title: Israel announces it owns the four Samuel scrolls
note: Prime Minister Moshe Sharett revealed the purchase, reuniting all seven original Cave 1 scrolls in Israel, and proposed a special building to house them.

title: Shrine of the Book opens
note: The Israel Museum's white-domed shrine, shaped after the lids of the scroll jars, opened to house the Cave 1 scrolls.

title: Temple Scroll recovered from Kando
note: During the Six-Day War, officers sent by Yigael Yadin went with the dealer Kando to Bethlehem on the evening of 8 June and recovered the longest Qumran scroll, hidden under his floor.
source: Silberman, A Prophet from Amongst You

title: Roland de Vaux dies
note: The Dominican scholar who excavated Qumran and led the official scroll team died with his final excavation report still unpublished.

title: Yigael Yadin dies
note: The soldier and archaeologist who secured four Cave 1 scrolls and the Temple Scroll for Israel died aged 67.

title: Computer-reconstructed scroll texts unveiled
note: Ben Zion Wacholder and Martin Abegg announced texts rebuilt by computer from the official team's concordance, published by the Biblical Archaeology Society, breaking the monopoly on unpublished Cave 4 material.

title: Huntington Library opens its scroll photographs to all
note: The Huntington announced it would let any qualified scholar consult its full set of master photographs of the scrolls, effectively ending restricted access.

title: BAS releases the facsimile edition of unpublished scrolls
note: The Biblical Archaeology Society published nearly 1,800 photographs of unpublished fragments in two volumes edited by Eisenman and Robinson.

title: Jerusalem court rules for Qimron over the MMT text
note: Judge Dalia Dorner held that Elisha Qimron owned the copyright in his reconstruction of the Halakhic Letter (4QMMT), which BAS had printed without permission. News reports appeared on 31 March.

title: Israel's Supreme Court upholds Qimron's copyright
note: A panel led by Aharon Barak upheld the 1993 verdict that a scholar's reconstruction of a scroll text is protected work. Reported in the New York Times on 31 August.

title: Israel Museum and Google put five scrolls online
note: High-resolution, searchable images of the Great Isaiah Scroll and four other Cave 1 scrolls went live. Wikipedia gives 25 September; contemporary reports say 26 September.

title: Leon Levy Dead Sea Scrolls Digital Library launches
note: The Israel Antiquities Authority, with Google, launched its online library of thousands of fragment images in colour and infrared.

title: En-Gedi Leviticus scroll read by virtual unwrapping
note: A team led by Brent Seales published scans revealing Leviticus text inside a charred scroll from En-Gedi, the oldest Pentateuch scroll found since Qumran.

title: Twelfth Qumran scroll cave announced
note: Hebrew University and Israel Antiquities Authority archaeologists reported a cave that once held scrolls, with jars, wrappings, a blank parchment and pickaxes left by looters.

title: Museum of the Bible says five fragments are forgeries
note: Tests by Germany's Federal Institute for Materials Research led the museum to withdraw five of its sixteen "Dead Sea Scroll" fragments as probable modern fakes.

title: All sixteen Museum of the Bible fragments found to be fake
note: An independent investigation presented at a museum conference concluded that every one of its sixteen fragments was a modern forgery on ancient leather.

title: IAA unveils new scroll fragments from the Cave of Horror
note: The Israel Antiquities Authority presented about 80 new pieces of a Greek Minor Prophets scroll, the first new biblical scroll fragments found in excavation in some 60 years.

title: Enoch AI study redates many scrolls earlier
note: Mladen Popovic's team combined new radiocarbon tests with machine-learning handwriting analysis, concluding that many scrolls are older than thought and two biblical fragments come from their books' traditional era.
